body:
Arjun Desai: Want to lock in a weekly publishing cadence for the Quantization Profile Library so we don’t end up drip-publishing random profiles. Proposal: ship profiles on a fixed day each week + clear labels (experimental vs stable) + deprecation policy. Need decisions today so registry + docs can align.

Marissa Cole: +1. also: cadence has to work for beta design partners. They’re asking “when will model X get a profile” and “will recommended change under me.”

Karthik Iyer: What are we optimizing for? If it’s trust, weekly is good but only if quality gates are strict. Otherwise we’ll get “new profile broke my route.”

Jonas Weber: For evals: we can realistically run full suite on 2–4 model variants/week, assuming prompt sets + perf suite + stats review. More than that and we’ll start cutting corners.

Selene Huang: Guardrails angle: labeling has to be enforceable by policy engine. I don’t want “experimental” to be a docs-only flag. If experimental, we should require explicit enable + maybe block for certain tiers unless allowlisted.

Paula Mendes: Telemetry/rollout: weekly drops should come with a standard dashboard annotation + changelog entry. Also a deprecation window so we can alert tenants who still pin deprecated refs.

Quentin Harris: Registry can support: status enum (experimental/stable/deprecated), published_at, deprecated_at, and “superseded_by” references. But keep in mind: values need to be immutable once published except deprecation metadata.

Olivia Grant: Eval harness can tag runs by profile_id and emit a “publishable” verdict, but we need a single source of truth for what “pass” means for experimental vs stable.

Sana Farid: For stats: I’d like two tiers:
- Experimental: must pass non-inferiority on core sets with looser threshold + wider CI allowed.
- Stable: must pass across the full required suite + stricter thresholds, and no single task family regression beyond guardrails.
Also: define minimum sample sizes so weekly cadence doesn’t become “we only tested 20 examples.”

Arjun Desai: Concrete cadence proposal:
- Every Tuesday 10am PT: publish new profiles to library (status=experimental by default)
- Promote experimental->stable the following Tuesday after at least 1 week of perf-canary + no guardrail alerts
- Deprecate older stable profile versions when superseded, with 30-day deprecation window before removal
Thoughts?

Jonas Weber: Tuesday works. But promotion after exactly 1 week might be too rigid. Some models need more soak time (decode latency tails). Maybe “min 7 days, max 21 days” depending on signals.

Selene Huang: +1, and promotion criteria should include: fallback_rate < X, no “quality regression” alerts, and p95 latency delta within SLO bands for the canary routes.

Marissa Cole: We should clarify “publish” vs “recommended alias update.” I’m ok publishing experimental weekly, but changing `recommended` weekly without customer action is scary.

Quentin Harris: Agree. Registry can support aliases (`recommended`, `latest_stable`, `latest_experimental`) but I’d strongly suggest we only advance `recommended` when we promote to stable, and even then maybe require an explicit change control step.

Paula Mendes: From UX: Console will show a list of profiles; most customers will choose by name. But some will just pick recommended. We should avoid a situation where “recommended” flips and their route changes behavior.

Arjun Desai: So:
- `latest_experimental` can move weekly (opt-in only)
- `latest_stable` can move when stable promotion happens
- `recommended` should be pinned per model variant for longer? like monthly or only on explicit “release notes” cycle?

Karthik Iyer: I’d vote `recommended` = stable and only moves when we have high confidence + explicit comms. Weekly is too often.

Elliot Price: Docs perspective: “experimental” needs a plain-language definition + disclaimer + best practices (run A/B evals, monitor fallback/latency). Also we need to document deprecation: what happens if you’ve pinned a deprecated profile ref.

Sana Farid: For deprecation policy, please don’t hard-remove without a loud warning. We’ll need to keep eval reproducibility. If a customer files a ticket “quality changed,” we’ll want to reproduce with the exact profile version.

Quentin Harris: We can keep artifacts indefinitely (or longer retention) even if deprecated, but we might want to disallow *new* enables after a “sunset” date.

Selene Huang: Yes: deprecated should mean “still works if you’re pinned” but Console/API warns and we block selecting it for new routes unless a special override.

Olivia Grant: Implementation detail: policy engine should treat deprecated as incompatible unless currently pinned? That’s a little subtle.

Quentin Harris: Better: policy engine returns a warning state for deprecated on read; on write, validator rejects selecting deprecated unless `allow_deprecated=true` (internal only). For already-configured routes, we let it resolve but emit a metric + warning in Console.

Jonas Weber: Model coverage per week: I’d prefer we commit to a small set of “top traffic” models first. Like 70B class and 8B class that we know customers run. We can publish a coverage sheet but keep it honest.

Marissa Cole: Product asks: can we say “new profiles weekly for our top open models” and publish a public-ish roadmap? At least for beta partners.

Arjun Desai: For initial weekly targets (next 4 weeks):
- llama-3.1-8b-instruct (INT8 weight-only + FP16 acts)
- llama-3.1-70b-instruct (FP8 mixed)
- qwen2.5-7b-instruct (INT8)
- mistral-large-2 (FP8 mixed) (if runtime ready)
These are tentative, gated by compatibility/perf.

Jonas Weber: I’m good with that list, but mistral-large-2 FP8 mixed is the riskiest. Might slip.

Karthik Iyer: We should define “experimental” for customers as: “may change without notice” vs “published but not recommended.” Please don’t say “may change” if IDs are immutable.

Elliot Price: Yeah. Better wording: “Experimental profiles are published and versioned, but may show higher variance in quality/latency across workloads. Use only with evaluation + monitoring. Not covered by our standard performance expectations.” (Something like that.)

Paula Mendes: Also: weekly publish should include a changelog line with expected savings bands (cost/token delta range) and known caveats (seq len caps, GPU constraints).

Selene Huang: +1 and include the “max context” / “unsupported GPU SKU” restrictions prominently. That’s where people get hurt.

Arjun Desai: Ok, let’s lock decisions:
1) Publish cadence: weekly (Tues 10am PT) for new profiles (usually experimental)
2) Promotion: experimental -> stable after min 7 days soak + passing metrics (quality + latency + fallback) and signoff from Applied ML + Runtime + SRE
3) Aliases:
- `latest_experimental`: can move weekly
- `latest_stable`: moves on promotion
- `recommended`: moves on an explicit, less frequent release (monthly-ish) with release notes; not automatically weekly
4) Deprecation:
- When stable profile superseded, mark old as deprecated
- Deprecated remains resolvable if pinned
- Console/API blocks selecting deprecated for new routes (unless internal override)
- 30-day deprecation window before “sunset” (disallow new enables + strong warnings). Artifacts retained for reproducibility.
Sound right?

Jonas Weber: Works for me. Add: if guardrail alert fires, we can immediately set `status=deprecated` (or `blocked`) and force fallback. But we may need a separate “blocked” state.

Quentin Harris: We can add `status=blocked` as a hard stop (not selectable, not resolvable unless internal). But schema change is heavier. Alternative: keep status=deprecated + add `resolve_allowed=false` flag.

Selene Huang: I prefer “blocked” conceptually, but we can do `resolve_allowed=false` for v1. Semantics: deprecated = soft, resolve_allowed=false = hard stop.

Paula Mendes: For dashboards, I’ll add a panel: “profile_resolution_outcome by profile_id” so we can see if a profile is being force-fallbacked.

Redwood Release Bot: Reminder: Release train cut for next week is Monday 5pm PT. Any schema changes after that may slip to following week.

Arjun Desai: Given release train note, we’ll keep it simple for v1: status {experimental, stable, deprecated} + `resolve_allowed` boolean for emergency blocks.

Marissa Cole: Please make sure Console copy differentiates deprecated vs blocked. If we overload deprecated, customers won’t understand why it suddenly doesn’t apply.

Elliot Price: Noted. I’ll draft copy:
- Deprecated: “still supported for existing routes; new use discouraged”
- Blocked: “disabled due to regression; will not apply; route will fall back to baseline.”

Olivia Grant: I’ll update eval playbook to reflect promotion criteria and minimum soak window.

Sana Farid: I’ll send thresholds proposal for experimental vs stable by EOD, so we can reference it in the publishing checklist.

Arjun Desai: Great. I’ll update the internal publishing checklist doc + coverage sheet with “weekly Tuesday drops” and the alias semantics. Thanks all.
